title: Two Sum
description: Find two numbers that add up to a specific target.
inputFormat:
Line 1: Integer n (number of elements)
Line 2: n space-separated integers
Line 3: Target integer
outputFormat: Standard output stream containing the computed result.
whyLearnThis: Essential lookup optimization problem; reduces O(N^2) brute force to O(N) using Hash Map.
recognitionClues: Look for array/string traversal where hashing properties or sliding boundaries reduce time complexity.
concepts: Complement Search, Hash Map constant-time lookup

examples.explanation: pair is not at the start. Expected output: [1,2]

hints: Can you check if target - current_element exists?
Use a hash map to store visited elements and their indices.
Single pass: look up target - nums[i] in map before inserting nums[i].
approach: Iterate through array. For each num, calculate complement = target - num. If complement in map, return indices. Otherwise insert num -> index.
intuition: By maintaining optimal state or invariants during iteration, we avoid recomputing redundant subproblems.
algorithm:
1. Initialize data structures (Array, Hash Table).
2. Traverse input while updating current boundary or accumulator.
3. Return result once target state is reached.
commonMistakes: Re-using the same element twice, not checking if complement is already stored.
edgeCases: Duplicate numbers that add up to target, negative numbers.
interviewTrick: Focus on invariant preservation and spatial optimization (in-place manipulation where applicable).
revisionNotes: Key Hashing question frequently asked in FAANG/Top Tech interview loops.
